gaps: The FCC internal photos and block diagram are metadata only, so they were not read.
The article's introduction describes a single 10000mAh ATL cell, while its teardown shows two 5000mAh cells in series.
method: ChargerLAB teardown of the A110Z: two ATL 606072G 5000mAh cells in series (39.1Wh rated), INJOINIC IP5385 master chip, CPS WB8118 wireless transmitter, LEADTECK MOSFETs.
FCC ID 2AOKB-A110Z is listed for model A110Z.

comps.spec: Two ATL 606072G cells, each 5000mAh (19.55Wh) at 3.91V nominal, connected in series. Article rated energy 39.1Wh; article says the pack delivers an equivalent 10000mAh capacity.
INJOINIC IP5385 built-in power bank master control chip. Article says it supports two USB-A output ports and a bidirectional USB-C port.
comps.loc: Master PCBA, back side (article back-side list)

comps.spec: CHIPSEA CBM8580KCV lithium battery protection chip (article caption). The article summary also calls it an advanced BMS fuel gauge.
Two LEADTECK LT7401FLCB lithium battery protection MOSFETs (article caption).
NTC thermistor for monitoring the temperature of the battery pack (article caption; no part number given).
comps.loc: Battery pack (exact board position not stated)

comps.spec: Nickel strips of the battery cells, welded by ultrasonic spot welding on the back (article text).
Blue plastic core USB-C port (article caption); no maker or part number given.
8.2μH alloy choke, no part number given (article).
comps.loc: Not stated in source (article front-side list names chokes; this one not located)

comps.spec: SOUTHCHIP SC8329 synchronous step-up chip for the wireless charging boost (article caption). Article says its switching frequency is 200kHz-2.2MHz, adjustable by an external resistor.
CPS WB8118, which the article describes as a high-efficiency magnetic induction wireless power transmitter IC (wireless charging chip).
Wireless charging coil, tightly wound with Litz wire, with a magnetic shielding sheet on its back. No part number given.
NTC thermistor on the wireless charging coil, to monitor charging temperature and prevent overheating (article).
Four LEADTECK LTS7906FL synchronous buck-boost MOSFETs (article caption).
LEADTECK LT3810FPJ VBUS MOSFET (article caption).
Two power supply control MOSFETs marked 4801, from LEADTECK (article caption).
LEADTECK LTS1582FPC, dual NMOS 60V and 11mΩ (article). Used for wireless charging resonant cap switching.
CHIPSEA CS32L015K8V6 MCU that drives the digital display screen (article caption).
comps.loc: Not stated in source (article back-side list names an MCU)

comps.spec: UCUNDATA UC25HD40 memory chip (article caption).
40MHz crystal oscillator that generates the clock signal (article caption); no marking given.
Digital display screen, described by the article as hidden on the side of the unit; driven by the CHIPSEA CS32L015K8V6 MCU.
Power button, located on the side of the unit (article). No part marking given.
Two 25V 100μF capacitors from LIANG HUA (article text). The article does not state the capacitor type.
